description: The one runtime policy every DwarfStar model uses. A model file in config/models may override a model_defaults key only with a reason in its override_reasons; repeating a default is rejected.

cache.policy: fixed by the runtime's Qwen4Exp graph (K/V allocated and read as F16; no quantized KV path). Q8 KV is future runtime and kernel work.

runtime.attention: the runtime's fused Metal attention kernels; always on (no switch exists)
runtime.weights: memory-mapped GGUF with Metal residency requested at load; no mlock flag in the runtime
runtime.gpu_offload: full: every layer, the MTP head and the vision projector run on the Metal GPU
runtime.ple: n-gram table read from disk row by row, never resident
runtime.threads: runtime default (GPU-bound; no CPU thread tuning)
runtime.mtp: native multi-token prediction on, adaptive depth, per-request timing
runtime.vision: projector loaded at start and resident
runtime.batch: one request at a time per model; prefill in chunks of prefill_chunk tokens
runtime.output_reservation: the server budgets decode against the exact remaining context; max_output is the per-request ceiling
runtime.telemetry: optional hooks; nothing is produced unless a Workstation subscriber asks (UDP 8039 events, 8037 detail heartbeats)
runtime.logging: one server log per start in the model's state directory; lifecycle journal in <data>/logs/lifecycle.jsonl

lifecycle.reasoning_change: same model: no restart; the effort is carried per request by the agent's provider file
lifecycle.ownership: the controller records pid, process birth and argv hash; it signals only that exact process

memory.formula: planned = resident model (main file + MTP head) + KV cache at the configured context + graph buffers at the prefill chunk + vision projector; required = planned + system reserve
memory.metal_working_set: the GPU's recommendedMaxWorkingSetSize, read from Metal on this machine; a model whose plan exceeds it fails at depth even when unified memory is free
memory.switching: a switch stops the running model first, so its planned memory counts as available for the target
